title: Endpoint IO-mode Breakout Grid: per-model/route p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs non-streaming cohorts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a compact, interactive grid dashboard that surfaces per-model and per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and error rates with an explicit split for streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes. This dashboard should help SREs and model owners quickly identify regressions tied to IO-mode behavior, understand distribution shifts, and trace into request-level spans when needed.

Background: Existing latency boards show percentiles but lack a concise cross-cut that highlights how streaming requests differ from blocking requests for the same model and route. Streaming behavior often has different performance characteristics (initial chunk latency vs steady-state token emission) and can mask regressions when aggregated. We need a grid that supports fast filtering by time window, model version, route tag, request shape cohorts, and streaming sentinel.

Data sources:
- Traces via trace-sampling hooks instrumented in the serving runtime (span tags: model, route, io_mode=streaming|sync, seq_len, seq_in_shape).
- Metrics from the metrics pipeline (histogram/tdigest for latency, counters for error types) emitted to our timeseries store.
- Logs for error classification (structured logs with request_id, model, route, io_mode).

Design & visualization:
- Primary view: grid where rows are models (or model family) and columns are routes (or route groups). Each cell shows compact sparkline + three percentile numbers (p50/p95/p99) split into two columns per percentile: streaming | non-streaming. Color heatmap overlay for p95.
- Hover panel: top contributing traces (sampled) for that cell and quick links to trace view and the related search query pre-populated in Logs Explorer.
- Cohort selector: request-shape buckets (short < 64 tokens, medium 64-512, long > 512) and ability to toggle include/exclude cached responses.
- Time comparison: baseline vs current window comparison with percentage change and statistical significance test (bootstrap on t-digest approximations).

Implementation plan:
1) Instrumentation changes (runtime): add io_mode tag to span root and ensure initial-chunk timing emitted as span.attribute "first_chunk_ms". (Owner: Miguel)
2) Metrics pipeline: emit separate histograms for latency_by_io_mode and update ingestion parser to populate t-digest tags. (Owner: Data Infra)
3) Logs: enrich error logs with io_mode and route labels for easier correlation. (Owner: Backend Logging)
4) Dashboard: Grafana/Console implementation that reads percentiles from timeseries store and links to Trace UI and Logs Explorer. Implement UI cells and hover actions. (Owner: Observability UI)
5) QA & rollout: validate against synthetic workload (streaming emulator) and a subset of production traffic via canary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard renders grid for top 50 models and top 20 routes within 10s for a 1h time window.
- Percentiles (p50/p95/p99) displayed per-cell for streaming and non-streaming and align within 5% of ad-hoc t-digest queries run in the analytics notebook.
- Hover links open trace view with pre-filtered request_id list and io_mode tag applied.
- Unit/integration tests added for ingestion changes; rollout gated by canary which shows no increase in metric ingestion latency > 2s.

Non-goals: creating a full per-token emission analyzer (out of scope for this ticket) or implementing new sampling policies for traces (sampling follow-up ticket).

Notes: keep instrumentation minimal to avoid increased CPU on hot request path; prefer non-blocking span attribute population. Use existing metrics prefixes to avoid pipeline rewrite.
